To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CO binds to Ag(001) through donation and back-donations, and the C-O stretch frequency is sensitive to the intermolecular coupling.
the CO-CO interactions are mediated by the surface and that the dispersion of the CO stretch mode is due to the coupling of CO with the surface.

(1) CO adsorbed on Ag(001), although the weakest of all the transition and noble metals, is bound by donation and back-donor interactions, (2) CO-CO coupling is mediated by the Ag substrate and is much stronger on Ag(001); and (3) the C-O stretch frequency dispersion is caused by the coupling of CO and Ag.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the bonding of a c(4×4)-CO overlayer to the Ag(111) surface, with the origin of the C-O stretching mode dispersion, and with the role of the metal in mediating intermolecular forces.
the nature of the bonding of CO and its vibrational properties on Ag(001).
the nature of the interaction of molecules with metal surfaces, and how it affects the molecular properties and the electronic and structural properties of the metal surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CO adsorbs on Ag(001), and the intermolecular coupling between COs is surface-mediated.
the nature of CO binding to Ag is very similar to that on other metals and that the CO-Ag coupling is the origin of the intermolecular coupling.
the CO-CO interactions are not direct, but are mediated by the Ag(001) surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ag-CO interaction is strong, but the CO-CO interaction is stronger.
the Ag-CO interaction is strong enough to cause the dispersion of CO-CO force constants but is too weak to cause a dispersion in Ag-CO stretch modes.
the nature of the CO-Ag(001) interaction, the dispersion of the CO-CO stretch mode, and the charge density response around adsorbed CO are all consistent with the Blyholder picture.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nature of the bonding of the c(2× 2)CO/Ag(001) is similar to that of other c(2×1) and c(4×2) CO overlayers on transition metal surfaces, with the exception that CO is bound more weakly on Ag(001).
the intermolecular coupling in CO/Ag(0001) is not due to the direct interaction between the molecules but rather is mediated by the metal.
the nature of the bonding of the adsorbate to the surface can be used to predict the nature of the intermolecular coupling and the dispersion of the adsorbates’ vibrational modes.
